Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Launch a Jupyter Lab server reachable from a remote browser.
#
# Usage:  scripts/notebook_server.sh [port]     (default: 8888)
#
# Needs only `uv` on the host: uvx downloads and caches JupyterLab on the
# first run, so there is no permanent install. The server binds 0.0.0.0 and
# the script prints the token URL to open from another machine.
set -euo pipefail

PORT="${1:-${PORT:-8888}}"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"

# Random token, printed once here so the remote URL is complete.
TOKEN="$(od -An -N24 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')"

# This machine's LAN IP, for the URL a remote browser should use.
IP="$(ip route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<NF;i++) if($i=="src") print $(i+1)}')"
IP="${IP:-$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')}"

echo "Open from a remote browser:"
echo "  http://${IP}:${PORT}/lab?token=${TOKEN}"
echo "CSR coverage sheet directly:"
echo "  http://${IP}:${PORT}/lab/tree/docs/csr_coverage.ipynb?token=${TOKEN}"
echo

exec uvx --from jupyterlab jupyter-lab \
    --ip 0.0.0.0 --port "$PORT" --no-browser \
    --IdentityProvider.token="$TOKEN" \
    --notebook-dir "$REPO_ROOT"
